questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

The burning of the effigy of Ravana on Dussehra ______ the burning of all evils.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

*The burning of the effigy of Ravana on Dussehra **symbolizes** the burning of all evils.*

**Symbolizes** means **be a symbol of.**

It is clear that **symbolizes** is the correct word as the sentence means that the burning of the effigy of Ravana on Dussehra is a symbol of burning evils.

**Intensifies** means **to become or make more intense.**

**Epitomizes** means **be a perfect example of.**

**Personifies **means **represent (a quality or concept) by a figure in human form.**

So, options **2,3 and 4 **are** incorrect.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. Mango, the so-called "king of fruits", is something of a national obsession in India.

B. There was a bumper crop of mangoes in different states.

C. It resulted in prices coming down and sales going up – much to the delight of buyers and sellers alike.

D. 2017 proved to be a very good year for mango lovers.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

The first statement should be **A** i.e. ''* Mango, the so-called "king of fruits", is something of a national obsession in India.*'' This is because it gives a suitable **introduction about what is going to be talked about in the following statements.**

After A it should be **D**, i.e '' *2017 proved to be a very good year for mango lovers*.'' This is because **B and C** seem to be in continuation with another statement.

After **D** it should be **B** as it gives the reason as to why 2017 was a good year for mango lovers.

The correct order is **ADBC.**

So, options** 2,3 and 4 are **incorrect.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

At night, lock the outer gate.

options.text: The outer gate is locked at night.
The outer gate is requested to be locked at night.
Let the outer gate be locked at night.
The outer gate be locked at night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Let the outer gate be locked at night__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an imperative sentence in active voice.
 
• **Sentences that express request, order, advice, suggestion, prohibition, etc., are called imperative sentences.__**
 
• **The imperative sentence in the passive voice has the following structure:**
 
 
• Let + object + be + past participle
 
 
 
• When the active voice begins with do not, the passive voice has the following structure:
 
 
• Let not + object + be + past participle
 
 
 
• 
 
Example:

 **Active:** Bring it home.

 **Passive:** Let it be brought home.

 
 
• 
 
**Thus, the passive voice for the given sentence is: ***Let the outer gate be locked at night.*

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Cyclone Idai is regarded as one of the worst tropical cyclone on record to affect Africa and the Southern Hemisphere as a whole.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the worst tropical cyclone**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **'One of the worst tropical cyclones' **should be there in place of **'One of the worst tropical cyclone'**
 
• The 'one of' is a singular term and generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.
 
• The noun or a pronoun used after the phrase “one of” is always in the plural form.
 
• The helping verb will always be in the singular form, as the helping verb agrees with “one of” and not with the plural noun in the sentence.

 Example: *One of the students was selected to visit NASA.*

Thus, the correct sentence is: *Cyclone Idai is regarded as one of the worst tropical cyclones on record to affect Africa and the Southern Hemisphere as a whole. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

There is hope that better forestry management will help in the ______ of the wildlife that is constantly facing threats because of increasing human activities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**conservation**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] **__

 
• **Meaning of the words given in the options are:**

 
 
• **Salvation** means preservation or deliverance from harm, ruin, loss, and the restoration of the natural environment and of wildlife.
 
• **Guarding **means watch over in order to protect or control.
 
• **Supervision** means to observe and direct the execution of (a task or activity).
 
• **Conservation** means preservation, protection, or prevention of wasteful use of a resource.
 
 
 
• It is clear that conservation is the most suitable word while talking about wildlife or nature.
 
• So, options **1, 2 and 4 **are **incorrect.**

**Thus, the complete sentence is: ***There is hope that better forestry management will help in the conservation of the wildlife that is constantly facing threats because of increasing human activities. *

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Their children were brought up with great care.

options.text: They brought up their children with great care.
They had brought up their children with great care.
Their children brought them up with great care.
They have been bringing up their children with great care.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

***They brought up their children with great care.***

Firstly, we interchange the subject and the object. **They **will become the subject and **children** will become the object. In the given question, **were** is given, which means that the active form of the sentence is in the simple past tense, so we simply remove **were** and use the simple past tense of the main verb i.e **brought.**

So, options** 2,3 and 4 **are** incorrect.**
